title: paged-kv-cache: block manager reuse + pinning optimizations
author: Asha Raman
release_notes: Optimizes paged KV cache block manager for allocator reuse and pinning; reduces tail latency and memory churn. No public API changes.
description: Motivation: The paged KV cache block manager has been a source of tail-latency variance and memory churn under bursty workloads. Workloads with frequent short-lived sequences (chat/streaming) stress the allocator and cause unnecessary evictions of pinned blocks. This PR reduces allocator churn, improves reuse of page blocks across requests, tightens pinning semantics, and exposes metrics to track reuse/hit-rate. Summary of changes: 1) Introduce a per-worker block free list (lock-free single-producer single-consumer) to allow fast reuse of recently freed blocks without expensive heap ops. 2) Add a pin-count fast-path and TTL for soft pins to avoid immediate eviction of recently used blocks while keeping long-term eviction fairness. 3) Move block allocation hot path to use a slab-like pre-reserved arena for common small block sizes, falling back to global allocator for large allocations. 4) Enhance the eviction policy with age-aware heuristics so pinned-but-stale blocks are deprioritized when memory is constrained. 5) Add end-to-end metrics: block_reuse_rate, soft_pin_count, block_alloc_latency_p50/p95/p99, eviction_reason. 6) Add unit and integration tests, and microbench harness results. Design notes: - The per-worker free list is implemented as a bounded ring buffer (capacity tuned at startup by runtime flags). It is lock-free for the common push/pop pattern between owner thread and allocator thread. The global allocator remains the authority for capacity accounting to avoid leaks. - Soft pin TTL defaults to 5s (configurable via runtime flag) and keeps a lightweight timestamp on pinned blocks; repeated pins refresh TTL. - Slab arenas are sized per-device and per-model-class to reduce fragmentation; arenas are reserved on pool init. Benchmarks (internal synthetic load approximating chat streaming, 2048 token seqs, mix of warm/hot contexts): - Baseline (main): median alloc latency: 18us, p95 alloc latency: 120us, tail (p99): 310us, throughput (tokens/s): 1.00x - This PR: median alloc latency: 9us (-50%), p95: 45us (-62%), p99: 120us (-61%), throughput: 1.12x. Real workload can vary; we see the biggest improvement on high-concurrency small-chunk workloads. Checklist: - [x] Per-worker free list implementation - [x] Soft pin TTL and fast-path - [x] Slab arena allocation fallback - [x] Eviction policy heuristics - [x] Metrics and dashboards added - [x] Unit tests and CI - [x] Perf microbench harness run and results attached Commits (high-level): - 2f4b7a8: implement per-worker free list and fast-path reuse - 7a1d3c2: add soft pin TTL and pin-count optimizations - 9c3d55e: slab arena allocator and fallback path - 0b6e4fd: eviction heuristics and metrics emission - 1f8a2b1: tests, benchmarks, and docs for flags/metrics Files changed (high level): - runtime/kv_cache/paged/block_manager.rs (majority of logic) - runtime/kv_cache/paged/allocator.rs (slab arena + global fallback) - runtime/kv_cache/paged/pinning.rs (soft pin TTL, fast-path) - runtime/kv_cache/paged/metrics.rs (new metrics) - runtime/kv_cache/tests/block_manager_tests.rs (unit tests) - benchs/kv_cache/paged_reuse_bench.rs (microbench harness) - docs/ops/kv-cache.md (operational notes + flags) - rust-toolchain.toml (bump toolchain for small atomic APIs) - CI/workflows/kv-cache-perf.yml (added perf job) Review conversation (high-level): - Diego Martinez (reviewer): "Nice direction. Can you clarify how we avoid ABA on the lock-free ring buffer?" - Asha Raman (author): "We use a small version counter on the slot and single-producer single-consumer guarantees from the worker/allocator pairing. Added detailed comments and a small unit test that simulates concurrent push/pop." - Liam Chen (reviewer): "Eviction heuristics look good, but we should ensure pinned TTL doesn't cause memory to grow unbounded under continuous pinning. Can we add a circuit-breaker?" - Asha Raman: "Added a global soft-pin budget that will force demotion of oldest soft pins when budget exceeded; default is conservative and tunable via runtime flags." - Sofia Patel (approver): "Run the perf harness and upload results to the dashboard; otherwise LGTM." - CI bot: "kv-cache-perf job passed, but flakiness observed in allocator unit test on one run; rerun fixed it." CI summary: - linux-unit: pass - linux-integration: pass - kv-cache-perf: pass - lint: pass - cargo-audit: pass Merge: - merge_method: squash - merge_commit_sha: "a7c9d5b3f4c2e1d9b8f6a12345deadbeef001122" - merged_at: "2026-02-20" Notes for operators: - Default soft pin TTL can be tuned via --kv.paged.soft_pin_ttl (default 5s). - Per-worker free list capacity via --kv.paged.worker_free_list_capacity (default 256). - Added new metrics; dashboards need importing (docs/ops/kv-cache.md contains Grafana JSON link).
